extracted.intended_audience: ProofWiki editors / contributors (people editing ProofWiki pages)
extracted.subtask_description: House-style guidelines for writing and formatting LaTeX source on ProofWiki pages, covering spacing, bracket commands, aligned equations, and template-safe constructs. Intended to make source code easier to read, maintain, and correctly interpreted by ProofWiki templates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Space before variables and commands
rubrics_metrics.description: Each variable, and each command beginning with a backslash should be preceded by a space, except (for some unexplained result of evolution) when enclosing things in brackets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This makes the source easier to read and maintain. See instances on the page for examples. Note the caveat about not ignoring this spacing rule even when omitting braces for single-character arguments (see the Omit braces for single-character parameters guideline): e.g. prefer `\dfrac 1 2` to `\dfrac12` because the latter is significantly harder to interpret visually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \paren for parentheses/brackets
rubrics_metrics.description: When enclosing brackets around an object, always use the \paren { ... } command, for example `\paren {a + b}` rather than `(a + b)`.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using \paren ensures aesthetically sized brackets automatically; it is the recommended way to produce parenthetical grouping on ProofWiki pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid manual sizing commands (\big, \Big, \Bigg, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: There should be no need to use the commands \big, \Big, \Bigg etc. for specifying the sizes of parentheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using the \paren {...} technique will almost always automatically size the brackets aesthetically, so prefer \paren over manual sizing commands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place punctuation outside math environments
rubrics_metrics.description: Punctuation should appear (if it is really necessary) outside the \LaTeX{} environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: write `Hence $\map f {\sin x}$.` (produced by `$\map f {\sin x}$.`) rather than `Hence $\map f {\sin x}.$` (produced by `$\map f {\sin x}.$`). The period/full stop should be outside the math delimiters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omit braces for single-character parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: Single-character parameters to standard \LaTeX{} constructs need not be put in curly braces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer `\dfrac 1 2` over `\dfrac {1} {2}` — both produce the same output (`$\dfrac 1 2$`), but the former makes the source significantly easier to read. However, do not ignore the spacing rule: `\dfrac12` (no space) is harder to interpret visually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Align multi-equality equations using the {{eqn}} template and separate lines
rubrics_metrics.description: If an equation includes multiple equalities or inequalities, it is best to place each equality on a new line and use the provided {{begin-eqn}} / {{eqn}} / {{end-eqn}} template.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Within the {{eqn}} template: the section following `| l =` is a LaTeX environment for material to the left of the equals sign; `| r =` is for the right; `| ll =` and `| rr =` produce material further left and right respectively (the `ll` column is often used for an "implies" or "leads to" sign). All these LaTeX environments are already in \displaystyle mode, so do not include that command. The `| c =` section is NOT a LaTeX environment and can be used to add comments about the equation. Example usages and the overall template layout are given on the page. The operator shown between columns can be changed with `| o =` to show inequalities, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting conventions within {{eqn}} entries
rubrics_metrics.description: When entering an {{eqn}} environment, non-empty columns should be entered on separate lines with the `|` and `=` all aligned; every empty column should in general be omitted (except perhaps for `| c =` placeholders).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These conventions optimize readability. More options for the {{eqn}} template are on its dedicated page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid constructs that break the eqn interpreter (double braces, pipe characters)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not include two consecutive open or close curly braces `{{` or `}}` anywhere in your {{eqn}} templates; it will break the interpreter. Do not include the vertical line `|` (pipe) in LaTeX expressions within {{eqn}} as this also breaks the interpreter. In particular `\|` (used to produce `\|`) has the same problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Workarounds: put spaces between adjacent curly braces (`{ {` or `} }`) to avoid `{{`/`}}` tokens; use `\vert` (or `\lvert` and `\rvert`) instead of `|`, and use `\Vert` instead of `\|`. These caveats apply only within the {{eqn}} environment; elsewhere such constructs are fine. For consistency and to accommodate copy-paste, it is desirable to always use `\vert` and `\Vert`, and to insert a space between adjacent curly braces within LaTeX strings.
